extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and readers interested in cinematic/style-driven prose
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting 'cinematic' fiction that uses visual imagery and scene linkage while retaining the novelistic capacity for commentary and synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective pressure and focalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Filter descriptions through a character's perspective rather than presenting 'objective' visual data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show sensory and visual details as mediated by a character's viewpoint (focalization) instead of an impartial camera-eye; keep observations tied to the character's attention, knowledge, and temperament. Exemplars noted: Hemingway, Greene, Highsmith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compressed imagery and linkage of moments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use compressed imagery and link moments together rather than relying on exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer condensed, image-driven beats that accumulate meaning across a sequence; avoid long expository stretches that summarize or tell rather than enact. Place images so they build on one another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of negative capability
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The power of negative capability' — readers construct meaning from gaps and silences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately leave gaps, silences, and unspelled implications for readers to infer; resist over-explaining so that the narrative's affect and associations can arise from what is omitted as well as what is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right image in the right place in a sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The right image in the right place in a sequence' creates accumulated meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be intentional about image placement; a single well-chosen image can resonate differently depending on its position in a chain of moments. Sequence and context determine a detail's weight and associative power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modulate interiority carefully; keep it tight
rubrics_metrics.description: Modulate interiority carefully — keep it 'quite tight' and 'close to the incident.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit internal exposition and keep close to the immediate experience or event; interiority should illuminate the incident rather than distract with broad, generalizing commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'trite physicality' (mere transcript of the moving image)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Trite physicality' — passages that function as mere 'transcript of the moving image.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not render scenes as a literal shot-for-shot or caption-like transcript of visual movement. Avoid cliched, surface-level physical description that adds no interpretive or emotional weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control cinematic technique; avoid sapping vitality
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncontrolled cinematic technique can 'sap writing of vitality.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply cinematic devices with restraint and purpose; unmoored or excessive filmic maneuvers (quick cuts, montage-like lists, camera metaphors) risk dulling literary energy unless integrated with character and thematic intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve fiction's discursive/synthetic capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid privileging incident so heavily that literature loses its 'discursive power' — its ability to synthesize meaning alongside action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance faithful depiction of events with the novelistic ability to interpret, comment, and synthesize. Fiction should both portray moments and, through that portrayal, reflect on structures, meanings, and consequences rather than merely cataloguing action.
